result.summary: Calls SHA256AutoDetect during the startup initialization of bitcoin-util, bitcoin-tx, and bitcoin-wallet. This enables hardware-accelerated SHA-256 implementations on supported CPU architectures instead of falling back to generic software hashing.
result.problem: Standalone CLI utilities do not initialize kernel::Context, which is where SHA-256 hardware acceleration detection normally runs. As a result, operations like bitcoin-util grind, batch transaction signing in bitcoin-tx, and wallet operations run hashing routines on the slower generic fallback implementation.
evidence: Author benchmarks on an M2 Max show that 'grind is ~5x faster and signing 2000 P2PKH inputs with bitcoin-tx ~2.3x' (PR description and commit message)
result.card: Calls SHA256AutoDetect in bitcoin-util, bitcoin-tx, and bitcoin-wallet to enable hardware-accelerated SHA-256 routines. Currently, these standalone CLI tools do not initialize kernel::Context and inadvertently default to the slow generic SHA-256 implementation. The author reports a ~5x speedup for bitcoin-util grind and ~2.3x speedup for signing 2000 P2PKH inputs with bitcoin-tx on an Apple M2 Max.

risk.why: Incorrect initialization in standalone tools could cause runtime crashes or incorrect hashing output for CLI utility users.
